why: Ambiguous vinculum: read as (x-4)/(sqrt(x)+2) the numerator factors as (sqrt(x)-2)(sqrt(x)+2) so y = sqrt(x)-2 and dy/dx = 1/(2 sqrt(x)) = option C exactly; the rival reading (x-4)/sqrt(x+2) gives (x+8)/(2 (x+2)^(3/2)), which matches none of the four options (checked symbolically and numerically at x=3), and that asymmetry fixes the intended reading.
Quotient rule: [a(cx+d) - c(ax+b)]/(cx+d)^2 = (ad-bc)/(cx+d)^2; the cross terms acx cancel, leaving ad-bc, not ac-bd or ab-cd.
Quotient rule with u = 5 sin x - 2, v = 4 sin x + 3: numerator = cos x (20 sin x + 15 - 20 sin x + 8) = 23 cos x, so dy/dx = 23 cos x/(4 sin x + 3)^2.
g = h' = a cos x - b sin x and f = g' = h'' = -(a sin x + b cos x), so f + h = -(a sin x + b cos x) + (a sin x + b cos x + c) = c.
Continuity at x=2 gives 4a + 2b = 10 and matching one-sided derivatives gives 4a + b = 2; subtracting yields b = 8 and then a = -3/2.

Printed defect: both branches carry the condition x <= 0, which leaves f undefined for x > 0; adopting the evidently intended reading (second branch for x > 0), both branches give f(0)=1 so f is continuous, while the left derivative 2x + cos x at 0 equals 1 and the right derivative 2x - 2 at 0 equals -2, so f is not differentiable at 0.
Term-by-term, f'(x) = x^49 + x^48 + ... + x + 1 (the constant 1 differentiates away), which is 50 terms each equal to 1 at x = 1, so f'(1) = 50.
